result.rationale: The diff shows `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host with the right side coming from `uri.host`, which Ruby's URI parsing does not downcase (case is preserved per RFC). Neither the `before_validation` normalization (`sub!` calls) nor the validation regex downcases stored hosts either. So a mixed-case referer host fails to match a stored lowercase host, raising Discourse::InvalidAccess — a real behavioral defect introduced by this new model.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, the lookup is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` after `host = uri.host`. The diff does not explicitly downcase the RHS, so strictly speaking the query is only guaranteed case-insensitive if `uri.host` is already normalized to lowercase. The finding’s claim that uppercase referers “never match” isn’t verifiable from the diff alone (Ruby’s URI parser may downcase), but adding `host = host.downcase` would make the intent unambiguous and robust.
